why: The shape is the known cd-relative bypass a string deny rule cannot spell, but the tmpfs-over-seats mount makes the namespace empty for any spelling.
The plain absolute path is the shape a deny rule catches at engine layer, and the sandbox independently empties the same exact path inside the namespace.
The path barely exists as text before the shell builds it, so a string rule cannot match it, while the sandbox blocks by mount point no matter how the string is assembled.
The glob expands at open() time to the real path, defeating a literal deny rule, but the mounted-over directory contains no seat file for the glob to match inside the sandbox.
The find propagates the matched path to the kernel outside any rule text, but the tmpfs mount leaves the directory empty so the walker never finds a file to cat.
The resolver canonicalizes the path before use so a deny rule has no direct string to match, while the kernel mount makes the resolved-back namespace a sandbox-empty tmpfs.
